approach: We treat this as a full-release reproduction of C1 and do not reimplement or modify the authors' search, static checker, or exact oracle. A thin reproduce.py verifies the archived certificate's SHA-256, invokes the authors' pure-Python static checker and independent exact path oracle on certificates/V7_16_le28/select_7th_of_16_28cmp.rs, parses the computed worst-case depth, and writes results/metrics.json. The mandatory path uses only Python stdlib and takes seconds; Rust re-search/randtest and Lean kernel checks are optional and skipped because only python, pip, and git are available. The expected exact result is depth 28 for n=16, 1-based rank 7 / 0-based rank 6, with 329 functions. The checksum, checker, and oracle together pin C1; the Lean proof is recorded as not run rather than silently claimed.

files.purpose: Thin orchestrator: verify SHA-256 of the target certificate, invoke the authors' static checker and exact path oracle via subprocess using sys.executable -I, parse the computed worst-case depth/function count, enforce C1 checks, and write results/metrics.json plus an optional --smoke result. It must not modify or reimplement checker/oracle/search code.

config.scope: C1 only; C2-C7 are not required for the match target
config.checkout: use the existing clone at repo root; if absent, git clone into repo root

tolerance.note: the quantity is an exact integer depth; faithful reproduction must equal 28. Because the contract says any computed value above 28 must be recorded as failed, the effective acceptance is computed_worst_case == 28, not merely <= 30.8

config.input_domain: permutations of 0..15; certificate accesses inputs only by comparison (A10)
config.comparison_model: decision DAG depth; return costs 0, comparison costs 1 + max(branch costs) (R1/R7)
config.optional_rust_search: false (Rust toolchain not executable in this sandbox; only python/pip/git)
config.optional_rust_randtest: false (2*10^7 permutations would need rustc; A7 seed not needed)
config.optional_lean: false (R11 not run; Lean toolchain not available under the python/pip/git-only constraint)
config.optional_r16_analysis: optional; run code/analysis/structure/r16_check.py only if it has a trivial CLI and fits in seconds (R12)

steps: Setup: confirm the repository root contains certificates/V7_16_le28/select_7th_of_16_28cmp.rs, code/verifier/verify_rs_algorithm.py, and code/independent_checks/checker/pathcheck.py. If the checkout is absent, run git clone https://github.com/JCremerr/selection-7-of-16 into the working directory; otherwise use the existing clone. Do not pip-install anything.

Read-only inspect the authors' scripts and archived outputs: code/verifier/verify_rs_algorithm.py, code/independent_checks/checker/pathcheck.py, certificates/V7_16_le28/SHA256SUMS, verifier_output.txt, and randtest_output.txt. Determine the exact stdout labels for computed worst-case depth and function count so reproduce.py can parse them without changing the scripts.

Write reproduce.py at repo root. It must use pathlib to locate the repo root from __file__, use hashlib for SHA-256 (not the sha256sum shell command), use subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', ...]) for authors' Python scripts, and use json to write results/metrics.json.

Implement the checksum check: parse certificates/V7_16_le28/SHA256SUMS for the line matching select_7th_of_16_28cmp.rs, compute hashlib.sha256 of the file, require equality with the SHA256SUMS entry, and require the hex digest to start with eb8f064c12bb. Record the full digest and both match flags.

Implement the static-checker invocation: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', 'code/verifier/verify_rs_algorithm.py', 'certificates/V7_16_le28/select_7th_of_16_28cmp.rs', '--expect-n', '16', '--expect-i', '7', '--expect-worst', '28'], cwd=repo_root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600). Require exit code 0. Capture stdout/stderr in metrics.

Parse the checker stdout for the computed worst-case depth and, if printed, the function count. Use the exact labels discovered in step 2. Do not set the metric solely from --expect-worst; if the checker does not print a computed depth, rely on the independent oracle for computed_worst_case and record checker_output_has_depth=false.

Implement the exact path-oracle invocation: run from code/independent_checks/checker with the certificate path resolved absolutely, using subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', 'pathcheck.py', absolute_cert_path], cwd=oracle_dir, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600). Require exit code 0. Parse its computed worst-case depth and function count if reported.

Enforce consistency: require oracle computed depth == 28; require checker computed depth == 28 if the checker reports one; require checker_depth == oracle_depth when both are present. If a function count is reported by either check, require 329; if neither reports it, count Rust fn declarations in the certificate with a simple regex and record the source as 'regex', but do not let an auxiliary count mismatch override a correct depth without recording a warning.

Implement --smoke mode: verify SHA-256 and run only the static checker on the target certificate, parse depth 28, and write results/smoke_metrics.json. This proves path resolution, subprocess invocation, output parsing, and JSON writing without running the full oracle.

Implement full mode: run checksum, static checker, and exact oracle; create results/ if needed; write results/metrics.json with claim_id C1, certificate path, n=16, one_based_rank=7, zero_based_rank=6, expected_worst_case=28, computed_worst_case, unit='comparisons', passed=true iff all mandatory checks pass and depth==28, sha256, function_count, tolerance, per-check exit codes/stdout/stderr, and an optional_checks_not_run list for Rust search/randtest and Lean R11.

Exit 0 only when the claim is reproduced exactly (computed depth 28 and mandatory checks pass). If any mandatory check fails, write metrics.json with passed=false and a non-empty error field, then exit nonzero. Never fabricate a computed depth from the expected value.

Optionally run code/analysis/structure/r16_check.py if it exposes a simple CLI, to record the shared R16 opening check; this is auxiliary and must not block the C1 verdict. Optionally verify the alt 365-function certificate only if time remains.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: it should verify the SHA-256 of certificates/V7_16_le28/select_7th_of_16_28cmp.rs, invoke only the authors' static checker with --expect-n 16 --expect-i 7 --expect-worst 28, parse computed depth 28, and write results/smoke_metrics.json. This takes seconds and proves the data flow before the full oracle run.
intermediate_checks: Confirm the target certificate exists and is 89,947 bytes; compute SHA-256 and confirm the prefix eb8f064c12bb from Table 3 and the entry in SHA256SUMS.

Inspect the static checker's actual stdout on the target certificate. Confirm it exits 0 and prints a computed worst-case depth of 28; confirm whether it prints the function count 329. If it prints only 'OK', still require exit 0 and use the oracle for the numeric depth.
Inspect the exact oracle's actual stdout on the target certificate. Confirm it exits 0, enumerates all paths, and reports worst-case depth 28; record runtime.

Negative control: run the static checker with --expect-worst 27 on the same certificate and require a nonzero exit. If it still exits 0, stop and inspect the checker's semantics before trusting the positive run.
Check the rank convention: --expect-i is 1-based (7), while the certificate and Lean triple use 0-based rank 6. Verify the checker is invoked with 7 and metrics record both conventions.

Check function count: if checker/oracle reports 329, require 329. If not, count `fn` declarations in the Rust certificate with a regex and record the count/source; investigate any mismatch from 329 without silently changing the depth metric.

Confirm `python -I` works for both authors' scripts from the intended working directories (repo root for checker, code/independent_checks/checker for oracle) and that there are no missing imports or pip requirements.
Confirm results/ is writable and that all captured stdout/stderr strings are JSON-serializable (decode bytes with errors='replace').
Optional: run code/analysis/structure/r16_check.py if it has a simple CLI to sanity-check the 15-comparison R16 opening (R12); do not block on it.
budget_plan: About 20 minutes total: 0-3 min setup/clone/inspect authors' scripts; 3-8 min write reproduce.py; 8-9 min smoke run; 9-12 min intermediate checks including the wrong-expectation negative control; 12-15 min full run and metrics write; 15-20 min buffer for parser adjustments. The mandatory Python checker and oracle runs are seconds each. Do not spend budget on Rust or Lean toolchains; record them as optional checks not run.
